formats.key: swap(address fromToken,string toToken,string destination,uint256 fromAmount,uint256 minReturnAmount)
effects: The contract pulls exactly fromAmount of fromToken from the signer into the SWFT contract with transferFrom, using up that much of the signer's allowance to the contract.

Nothing else happens on-chain: the contract only emits a Swap event with toToken, destination and minReturnAmount. The payout in another asset, often on another chain, is made later and off-chain by SWFT, and the code enforces no minimum.
formats.shown: Send <fromAmount fromToken> to SWFT to swap for <order string>, paid to <payout address>, with a requested minimum in raw units, plus a note that payout is off-chain and the minimum is not enforced.

findings.title: swap: the requested minimum is a raw integer because the target token is only an off-chain string.
findings.evidence: SwftSwap.sol swap(): minReturnAmount is only emitted in the Swap event. descriptor: {"path":"minReturnAmount","label":"Requested Min (raw)","format":"raw"}. Case 0 shows '163481336' and the reader was unsure of the USDT decimals.
findings.fix: No token address exists in calldata to format it. The '(raw)' label and the not-enforced note are the best available.

findings.title: swap: toToken is a pipe-delimited SWFT order string that goes into the sentence unparsed.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent 'swap for {toToken}' renders 'swap for BNB(BSC)|zvcm92|0.02|bridgers|0' (case 1). The blind reader in case 1 read the 0.02 as the expected BNB amount. In cases 3 to 5 readers could not tell what 'zvcm92' and '0.015' mean.
findings.fix: ERC-7730 cannot split a string. A label such as 'Target token / SWFT order (token|channel|fee|route)' would help a little.

findings.title: swap: the Optimism deployment is verified as BridgersSwap, while metadata names the contract SwftSwap.
findings.evidence: contracts/10-0xc1d1.../src/BridgersSwap.sol: contract BridgersSwap, name = "Bridgers Swap1.1". descriptor metadata.contractName "SwftSwap". The logic of swap() is identical.
findings.fix: Optional: note that the Bridgers brand is the same SWFT service.

cases.notes: 1000 ARB out to the SWFT contract, shown exactly. The ARB allowance consumed to 0 is the spend of the shown transfer, merged into it.
15 USDt out, shown exactly. The reader misread the 0.02 in the order string as the payout amount, but that concerns the off-chain payout, not an on-chain effect.
2236.540972 OP out, shown exactly. The allowance spend is merged.
2905 USDT0 (Polygon USDT) out, shown exactly. The reader briefly mixed up the Tron payout address with a deposit address, but correctly understood the asset, amount and SWFT as recipient.

effects: The signer sends msg.value of the chain's native currency to the SWFT contract, which keeps it.
Nothing else happens on-chain: the contract only emits a SwapEth event. The payout in the target asset to destination is made off-chain by SWFT, and the code enforces no minimum.
formats.shown: Send <native value> to SWFT to swap for <order string>, paid to <payout address>, with a requested minimum in raw units, plus a note that payout is off-chain and the minimum is not enforced.

findings.title: swapEth: the requested minimum is a raw integer because the target token is only an off-chain string.
findings.evidence: SwftSwap.sol swapEth(): minReturnAmount is only emitted. descriptor: {"path":"minReturnAmount","label":"Requested Min (raw)","format":"raw"}. Case 8 shows '23102636' and the reader had to guess the TRX decimals.
findings.fix: No token address exists in calldata. Keep the '(raw)' label and the note.

findings.title: swapEth: the order string hides the destination chain, so 'swap ETH for ETH' looks odd to readers.
findings.evidence: Case 7 renders 'swap for ETH|6nu8wra5|0.020000000|bridgers|0' and the reader asked 'Why swap ETH for ETH... doesn't say which chains'. Case 6 shows 'ETH|zvcm92|0.02|bridgers|0'.
findings.fix: Strings cannot be parsed in ERC-7730. A clearer label for toToken (target token / SWFT order) is the only help available.

findings.title: swapEth: the Optimism deployment is verified as BridgersSwap, while metadata names the contract SwftSwap.
findings.evidence: contracts/10-0xc1d1.../src/BridgersSwap.sol: contract BridgersSwap. descriptor metadata.contractName "SwftSwap". The logic of swapEth() is identical.

cases.notes: 1.1871347 ETH out on Optimism, shown exactly.
